body.title: Implement validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope
body.summary: Add a private declarative (scopeType, scopeLevel) -> required/must-be-absent field table and one shared comparison engine in a new src/workflow/artifact-core/scope-checks.ts, then export validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope (each ScopeValidator-typed) as thin closures over that engine (alternative a1). Each validator first checks scope.scopeType matches its own dedicated literal, then the self-inclusive field-presence table, then calls sc6's validatePointerPath (from pointer-checks.ts) against every populated Pointer-typed field, folding any violation into the same ValidationResult.violations array.
acceptanceChecks: validateDesignScope/validateCodeScope return ok:false with a named violation when called on the wrong scopeType
A field required at the Scope's own declared scopeLevel being absent, or a field deeper than scopeLevel being populated, each returns ok:false with a named violation (self-inclusive chain, ac2)
An invalid (scopeType, scopeLevel) combination with no table entry returns ok:false naming the combination itself, not a field-level error
scope.tasks as an empty array at a scopeLevel requiring tasks is treated as absent
Both validators call validatePointerPath against every populated Pointer-typed field and fold ok:false violations into the same violations array (sc6 consumption, closes the cross-LLD security gap)
Neither validator performs file I/O itself

tests.name: validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope are exported with their documented signatures and enforce the field-presence table and sc6 path validation, with no file I/O
